binds.giver: a lord whose border village was burned
binds.village: a burned village on the border
binds.rival: the leader of another house of the giver's own realm
binds.enemy_realm: the realm the giver is at war with

stages.journal: {giver} wants proof that {enemy_realm} burned the farms of {village}.
stages.canvas: The lord is furious and certain: the enemy did this. He wants proof to lay before the realm and the council, so the war is pressed where it hurts.
facts: Farms around {village} were burned within the last weeks.
The lord is sure {enemy_realm} did it.
He wants proof he can show the realm.

{giver}: Farms around your village {village} were burned. You are sure {enemy_realm} did it and want proof to lay before the realm.

stages.journal: Ask the people of {village} who burned their farms.
stages.canvas: Shaken survivors, glad someone asks. Their answers do not quite fit the lord's certainty.
facts: The raiders came by night, few in number, well mounted.
They spoke the tongue of this realm, not the enemy's.
One survivor saw a torn surcoat left behind in a burned barn.

locals_of:{village}: Raiders burned your farms by night; there were few of them, well mounted.
Strangely, they spoke like folk of this realm, not like the enemy.
Someone found a torn surcoat in a burned barn and hid it, afraid of what it means.

stages.journal: Find the surcoat hidden in the burned barns of {village}.

narration.canvas: Among the ashes, the player is shown the hidden surcoat, in the second person.
facts: The surcoat bears the colours of {rival}'s house.
It is a household rider's coat, not a peasant's.
The raid was made to look like the enemy's work.

stages.canvas: The lord's certainty breaks. Anger turns inward, toward a man he sat beside at council. He must decide what to do with a truth that shames his own realm.
facts: The raiders wore the colours of {rival}'s house.
It was made to look like {enemy_realm}'s work.
The lord thanks the player for the truth, though it is not the one he wanted.

{giver}: The player has shown you a surcoat in {rival}'s colours from the burned barns of {village}. Your own realm's house burned your farms and blamed the enemy.

reward.memory: The player found that {rival}'s riders, not {enemy_realm}, burned {village}, and brought me the truth.

grudge.note: Inc 2: a grudge between NPCs needs its own ruling.

failure.memory: I asked the player for proof against {enemy_realm} over {village}; none came.
